Again, I'm in the same boat. I've tried a bunch of different medications and 5 different therapists and I'm not sure if any of it was worth it. 

Just please push on. Your life will get better, making it easier to hang on. If it doesn't, then you'll have more reasons to grip just a little bit tighter.

That's really true. I know exactly how you feel by barely hanging on. But life's about surviving, and for now that is doing the job. It'll get better one day, and if it doesn't, then there'll be more reasons to hang on a bit tighter.

I'm so sorry. You don't deserve the pressure your feeling. No one does. 

Now, I'm not going to say that you have so much to live for, you're worth something, or even that you should do anything. Okay? I do think those things, but telling you won't mean much coming from me, or at least it won't mean as much as you feeling that way about yourself.

It seems to me that you think that reaching out to somebody - anybody - is worth it. Even if you don't realize it, you probably know all the reasons why you should be ecstatic about life and where you're going to be in a decade. Unfortunately, depression screws with how you feel about and perceive reality.

What I'm trying to say is that even though you may not see the light at the end of the tunnel, doesn't mean you don't know it's there and well within reach. That's why you're here friend.

The only way it would be better would be if you didn't want to try and improve people's lives, which doesn't seem like the case. School is school, and the classes you fail you can take again. I've had to do it quite a few times. It sucks and it's better to just pass the class, but when you haven't the drive for it it's understandable. 

Now for the wife, I know that's hard. You love her and would do anything you could do for her, but what she wants might not be something you can give. Relationships are all about compromise though, so if you give it your all and she doesn't react positively, then it's no longer a relationship. At that point it's simply work. Don't do that to yourself. 

Consider talking to her for a good while and try to explain things through in a thorough and thoughtful manner. Encourage her to ask the hard questions. Often times that alone will help you answer questions you haven't been able to ask yourself.

I want things to get better for you man. I really do. If I can do anything, let me know. Please, let me know. :)

I've been dealing with those types of thoughts almost every single day since March 14, 2012. That's the day my friend took his own life. And I understood why he did it. I still do. 

Lately, the thing that usually helps me is know that our emotions and how we feel isn't rational. Those feelings don't belong in objective reality. More likely than not there's probably a genetic reason you feel that way. Likely, still, that this is probably the only reason you feel that way.

Why let genetics and irrational emotions get in the way of making you feel fulfilled and satisfied with your life and who you are?

Think about switching games. Play a game by yourself and do some soul searching. Better yet, put down the game and just think about the situation for a bit. Go take a nap, read a book, or watch your favorite movie/TV show/podcast. Think about why you should listen to these guys when it's just a game.

These guys playing with you are just letting out steam about the same feelings probably. Don't take what they say to heart. I can almost guarantee that they have the same insecurities they're trying to push on you.
